title: dedicated: autoscaler burst controls + utilization reporting improvements (v16)
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Dedicated fleets have continued to experience transient latency spikes during sudden demand bursts. Existing burst allowance logic allowed short bursts but lacked transparent utilization reporting for customers and operators. This PR implements tighter burst controls, per-fleet burst budgeting, and a new utilization reporting pipeline for Dedicated to make burst behavior observable and debuggable. Motivation: reduce OOM/backpressure events during aggressive traffic spikes, give SREs and customers clear visibility into burst consumption and autoscaler decisions, and provide knobs for conservative vs aggressive burst policies. Key changes: 1) autoscaler: add burst_budget bookkeeping (per-fleet, time-decayed) to cap instantaneous scale-ups and enforce burst tokens consumption; 2) rate-limiter: introduce burst-token checks before allocating new nodes; 3) metrics: emit dedicated.fleet.burst_tokens{fleet_id,policy} and dedicated.fleet.utilization{fleet_id,window} with 1m/5m aggregates; 4) reporting: aggregator service transforms raw counters into per-fleet utilization reports and exposes them via the Console API + telemetry; 5) config: new FleetAutoscaler policy fields (burst_max_tokens, burst_recovery_seconds, burst_behavior: [conservative|aggressive]); 6) docs and release notes. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-7823) - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] canary on staging fleet - [x] Console UI PR for metric charts (linked) - [x] observability dashboards updated - [x] rollout plan + feature-flag gating Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag "dedicated_burst_v2". Start with non-critical fleets (tag=canary), monitor two key dashboards (burst_tokens, fleet_utilization) and two alert rules (burst_token_depletion, sustained_high_util). If metrics stable for 72h, progressively enable for remaining fleets. Performance notes: microbenchmarks show <2% p99 allocation latency regression in the fast-path; overall end-to-end throughput improved under bursty load due to fewer OOM-restarts. Backwards compatibility: new FleetAutoscaler fields are additive and default to previous behavior. Follow-ups: - debug endpoint to dump per-fleet token state (ENG-7910) - improved UI controls for burst policy in Console - tighter guardrails for multi-tenant Dedicated clusters. Related: ENG-7823, ENG-7910, SUP-3412. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-7823/dedicated-burst-policy, staged perf report https://perf.internal.redwood/reports/1002345. Testing notes: ran full CI, added targeted integration test that simulates step-input load and asserts no more than configured burst_allocations in 10s window. A flaky e2e from previous run (canary-network-timeout) was retried and passed on rerun. This description contains implementation highlights and the rollout and monitoring plan in a single continuous string as required.
commits_summary: feat(autoscaler): burst budget bookkeeping and enforcement; feat(metrics): emit burst_tokens and fleet_utilization; feat(api): Console endpoints for fleet utilization; refactor(autoscaler): split decision path for burst vs steady-state; tests: add unit/integration tests for burst policy; docs: update dedicated autoscaler docs and release notes
review_comments: Diego Marin (reviewer): Left a couple of comments on the recovery path - what happens when recovery_seconds is very small and fleet constantly oscillates? Consider rate-limiting allocations per-cluster to avoid flapping.
Maya Patel (author): Good catch, added cluster-level backoff (in burst_budget.go) and a unit test that simulates oscillation. Note in design doc why we prefer token decay over windowed counters.
Hannah Kim (reviewer): Can we add a short note in the Console UI about metric semantics (tokens vs capacity)? Some customers might misinterpret high token counts as spare capacity.
Maya Patel (author): Updated Console UI tooltip and docs to clarify semantics. Also added an example policy snippet in docs.
Oleg Petrov (approver): Approving after nits addressed. Please ensure the canary script is used for initial rollout. Left approval in PR.
CI Bot: integration-tests retried once due to transient gRPC timeout; subsequent run passed.
merge_summary: Merged by squash on main. Merge commit: squash commit 'dedicated: autoscaler burst controls + utilization reporting (v16)'. Merged_at 2026-03-02. Changelog entry added to release-notes/2026-03-dedicated-burst.md
release_notes: Dedicated autoscaler: added burst budgeting, per-fleet burst controls, and utilization reporting. New FleetAutoscaler policy fields: burst_max_tokens, burst_recovery_seconds, burst_behavior. Improved stability during sudden traffic spikes and new Console metrics for visibility. Rollout behind feature flag 'dedicated_burst_v2' (staged).
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag 'dedicated_burst_v2' for canary fleets using infra/helm/dedicated-values.yaml entry. Watch alerts: burst_token_depletion and sustained_high_util. If regressions observed, toggle feature flag off to revert to previous behavior.
perf_summary: Under synthetic step-load tests, median allocation latency unchanged, p99 allocation latency increased by ~1.8% in worst-case microbenchmarks; end-to-end request latency during bursts improved due to reduction in OOMs and restarts. See perf report: https://perf.internal.redwood/reports/1002345
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: misconfiguration of burst_recovery_seconds could allow prolonged overcommit or oscillation. Mitigation: conservative defaults and cluster-level backoff; feature-flagged rollout and canary monitoring. Additional risk: customers may misinterpret new metrics; mitigation: UI tooltips and docs updates.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-7910 - debug endpoint for per-fleet token dump
Console-1234 - UI controls for burst policy
human_readable_summary: Adds per-fleet burst budgeting and utilization reporting; emits new metrics and Console endpoints; feature-flagged staged rollout; includes tests, docs, and dashboards.
